result.topic_en: Euler derives the recurrence by which the numerators and denominators of the convergents of a continued fraction are each formed from the two preceding ones, tabulates them, and begins computing the differences between successive convergents.
result.transcription:
) 140 (
numerator P huiusmodi habebit formam: $M + Np$, similique modo denominator $\mathfrak{P}$ hanc: $\mathfrak{M} + \mathfrak{N}p$, ita vt sit $\frac{P}{\mathfrak{P}} = \frac{M+Np}{\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p}$. In hac igitur forma loco $p$ scribamus $p + \frac{1}{q}$
vt obtineamus fractionem $\frac{Q}{\mathfrak{Q}}$, quae ergo, postquam supra et infra per $q$ multiplicauerimus, erit
$\frac{Q}{\mathfrak{Q}} = \frac{Mq+Npq+N}{\mathfrak{M}q+\mathfrak{N}pq+\mathfrak{N}} = \frac{N+(M+Np)q}{\mathfrak{N}+(\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p)q}$.
Nunc vt hinc sequentem fractionem $\frac{R}{\mathfrak{R}}$ obtineamus, loco $q$ scribamus $q + \frac{1}{r}$, et postquam supra et infra per $r$ multiplicauerimus oritur
$\frac{R}{\mathfrak{R}} = \frac{Nr+(M+Np)qr+M+Np}{\mathfrak{N}r+(\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p)qr+\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p}$, siue
$\frac{R}{\mathfrak{R}} = \frac{M+Np+(N+Mq+Npq)r}{\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p+(\mathfrak{N}+\mathfrak{M}q+\mathfrak{N}pq)r}$.
Cum igitur sit $P = M + Np$, $Q = N + (M + Np)q$, erit $R = P + Qr$. Simili modo cum sit $\mathfrak{P} = \mathfrak{M} + \mathfrak{N}p$ et $\mathfrak{Q} = \mathfrak{N} = (\mathfrak{M} + \mathfrak{N}p)q$ erit $\mathfrak{R} = \mathfrak{P} + \mathfrak{Q}r$. Sicque patet, quomodo quaelibet nostrarum simplicium fractionum ex binis praecedentibus facile formari possit.

§. 4. Ecce igitur demonstrationem satis planam et dilucidam regulae notissimae pro conuersione fractionis continuae in fractiones simplices, vbi tam numeratores quam denominatores secundum eandem legem ex binis praecedentibus formantur. Cum igitur pro ambabus primis fractionibus sit $A = a$, $\mathfrak{A} = 1$, tum vero $B = ab + 1$ et $\mathfrak{B} = b$, ex his duabus fractionibus sequentes omnes facili negotio formari poterunt. Quod quo clarius appareat singulis indicibus $a, b, c, d, e$ etc. fractiones respondentes ordine subscribamus

$a \quad b \quad c \quad d \quad e \quad f \quad g$
$\frac{A}{\mathfrak{A}} \quad \frac{B}{\mathfrak{B}} \quad \frac{C}{\mathfrak{C}} \quad \frac{D}{\mathfrak{D}} \quad \frac{E}{\mathfrak{E}} \quad \frac{F}{\mathfrak{F}} \quad \frac{G}{\mathfrak{G}}$
ac tam numeratores quam denominatores secundum eandem legem ex binis praecedentibus sequenti modo determinabuntur
Pro numeratoribus | Pro denominatoribus
$A = a$ | $\mathfrak{A} = 1$
$B = Ab + 1$ | $\mathfrak{B} = b$
$C = Bc + A$ | $\mathfrak{C} = \mathfrak{B}c + \mathfrak{A}$
$D = Cd + B$ | $\mathfrak{D} = \mathfrak{C}d + \mathfrak{B}$
$E = De + C$ | $\mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{D}e + \mathfrak{C}$
$F = Ef + D$ | $\mathfrak{F} = \mathfrak{E}f + \mathfrak{D}$
etc. | etc.
Vnde perspicuum est, in serie numeratorum terminum primo anteriorem ex lege progressionis esse debere $= 1$, in serie autem denominatorum terminum primo anteriorem esse debere $= 0$, ita vt fractio primam praecedens sit $\frac{1}{0}$.

§. 5. Quoniam per se satis est perspicuum, has fractiones $\frac{A}{\mathfrak{A}}, \frac{B}{\mathfrak{B}}, \frac{C}{\mathfrak{C}}, \frac{D}{\mathfrak{D}}$ etc. continuo propius ad veritatem accedere, ac tandem verum valorem fractionis continuae exhaurire, necesse est vt differentiae inter harum fractionum binas proximas continuo fiant minores, quamobrem has differentias ordine euoluamus. $II - I = \frac{B\mathfrak{A} - A\mathfrak{B}}{\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B}}$.

items.quote: Sicque patet, quomodo quaelibet nostrarum simplicium fractionum ex binis praecedentibus facile formari possit.
items.english: And thus it is clear how any of our simple fractions can easily be formed from the two preceding ones.

items.quote: Quoniam per se satis est perspicuum, has fractiones $\frac{A}{\mathfrak{A}}, \frac{B}{\mathfrak{B}}, \frac{C}{\mathfrak{C}}, \frac{D}{\mathfrak{D}}$ etc. continuo propius ad veritatem accedere, ac tandem verum valorem fractionis continuae exhaurire
